claims.text: How Does the USA Compare on HEALTHCARE?
claims.support: USA has the highest current health expenditure share of GDP at 16.7% (rank 1).
Refers to the range of health expenditure shares across countries in the World Bank indicator.

claims.text: Comparing health expenditure as a percentage of GDP across nations using World Bank data.
claims.support: Indicator SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS measures current health expenditure as % of GDP across 189 countries and territories.

claims.text: The United States spends 16.7% of its economy on health. Laos spends 1.3%.
claims.support: USA health spending display is 16.7% (16.69%) and Laos display is 1.3% (1.33%).

claims.text: That gives the United States the highest healthcare spending share on Earth.
claims.support: USA is ranked #1 out of 189 entities with 16.69% of GDP.

claims.text: Compare that to India, which spends 3.3% of its economy on health.
claims.support: India (IND) current health expenditure display is 3.3% of GDP (value 3.34%, rank 168).

claims.text: This counts healthcare goods and services consumed, excluding capital costs like buildings and machinery.
claims.support: Indicator definition states it includes healthcare goods and services consumed, excluding capital expenditures such as buildings and machinery.

claims.text: Near the top, Afghanistan spends 15%, Germany spends 12.3%, and the UK spends 11.1%.
claims.support: Afghanistan (AFG) display is 15% (rank 2), Germany (DEU) display is 12.3% (rank 7), United Kingdom (GBR) display is 11.1% (rank 14).

claims.text: At the very bottom sits Laos, spending just 1.3%.
claims.support: Laos (LAO) is ranked #189 out of 189 with 1.3% of GDP.

claims.text: How much of your nation's economy goes to healthcare?
claims.support: Closing prompt framing the World Bank indicator.
